source: សៀវភៅស្ដីពីដំណាំដំឡូងមី (Book on Cassava), Part 2, UNDP-supported capacity-building programme for cassava, March 2015, Sections 10.2-10.3
text:
The source describes a six-step process for an exporting company selling cassava to a new buyer (Table III-10.1): (1) the buyer researches the exporting company, compares prices among sellers, and makes contact - existing trusted relationships can shortcut this step; (2) the buyer checks product quality and price/terms, and may request samples before agreeing or negotiating new terms; (3) the exporting company confirms available stock and finalizes terms with the buyer; (4) once terms are agreed, the company prepares invoicing and delivery per the agreed schedule and quality requirements; (5) the company prepares export documentation; (6) the company arranges transport/shipping logistics.

The source also lays out the general legal framework for cassava export procedure, requiring compliance with (1) national production and phytosanitary standards, (2) national import/export law, and (3) applicable trade/tariff agreements (e.g., WTO, ASEAN, GSP).

A process diagram (Figure III-10.9, described as reflecting a 2013 industry survey) shows the export-certificate approval flow between the exporter and the General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA):
Exporter: (1) prepares documentation for the Export Certificate, submitting: owner(s)' biography/ID or passport, company registration, VAT and patent documents, office and warehouse/silo location details, factory location(s), and farm location(s).
GDA: (2) verifies the submitted documents - if incorrect, returns them to the exporter for correction; if correct, (3) assigns an inspector to conduct an on-site inspection, who (4) collects soil and commodity samples for laboratory testing. If no contamination is found, (5) the business is confirmed legitimate, and GDA (6) issues the Export Certificate and adds the company to its approved exporter list, then (7) the exporter collects the Export Certificate from GDA, and (8) GDA sends the approved-exporter list to China's CIQ (Commodity Inspection and Quarantine authority).
caveat: The process-flow diagram (Figure III-10.9) was presented in the source with English-language labels, which reduces transcription risk for this file compared to Khmer-only passages; it is reproduced here with reasonable confidence.
